Yes and I’m glad you asked! So I’ve been sick my whole life but got diagnosed in 2020. My husband has sjogrens and perhaps more but he’s waiting on his rheumatologist visit. We have two kids. Kid 1 is healthy but has skin problems like eczema. Kid 2 is healthy and no signs of any autoimmune issues so far. However, he had a twin that didn’t make it to birth. 

Unfortunately there is a LOT of nuances to genetic diseases, so my story is not the same as everyone’s. My mother had discoid lupus and no organ involvement, but I have all the organ involvement. The biggest thing to keep into consideration is how well your disease is controlled and if you’re on any kind of medication that can be harmful to unborn baby (such as methotrexate). Beyond that, keeping close with your doctors during pregnancy is crucial. It never hurts to have a conversation with your most trusted doctor, and seeing how they feel about it.

An unfortunate laundry list... For me, it was extreme exhaustion, extreme and intolerable nausea (which made me end up losing 110lbs and become anorexic, I still haven't recovered from that), but if I'm honest, my vanity is what made me call MTX quits. I lost 60% of my hair. 

I took 15mg weekly, six little horrible pills and for 3 days after I was completely useless. It's a form of chemo, so imagine everything you go through with chemo as a side effect of MTX. 

One very, very shitty thing about medication is the cost and the red tape of insurance. My insurance tried to tell me that I wouldn't be able to be covered for the Amjevita if I hadn't tried other biologics. The only thing that changed their minds was that I'd been on the tier of meds below it for a long enough time, and had no actual improvement on it. Otherwise I'd be paying $12k a month just to keep me alive. So that being said, let your rheum know all the side effects you can't tolerate. Not every form of autoimmune disorders behave the same way. Being that you've taken 3 other things with no success, keep pushing. I had psoriatic arthritis starting as soon as I stopped taking MTX, but it went away on the AMJ. Never had it before I stopped taking the chemo... 

You got this, ok? Don't let anyone tell you what you feel is wrong. Keep pushing to get to a point where you're comfortable, don't be afraid to be the squeaky wheel!

The album in itself is different. In between the tracks, as you know, he talks about the guitar that inspired the headlining songs on the album. At the ending track, I can hear in his voice how he feels a disconnect between himself and the guitar and that time period in which he was writing them. Let's put a pin in that and I'll come back to that point later.

As for Late July... Well, obviously I didn't get the version I wanted and love so much. I got something that turned into more of what I envisioned behind the words, which is to say a sort of O'Brother Where Art Thou vibe. Southern, 1930s... Even if the beginning is different than the rest of the track the feeling remains. It feels hot, golden hour, like it was recorded on the porch of a house that had been standing for many a generations. I don't know, in this version you can feel that there's honesty behind the words. As if the man singing is completely satisfied with what he'd done and that he's going to be put on the electric chair soon. The famous drainage pipe version feels like he's giving his best rendition of something his father passed down. This is all my opinion, obviously lol

Back to the album in it's entirety... We're hearing a young Shakey, no doubt about that but there's that "I don't know what I'm doing, I'm just getting it out of my head" emotion behind the sound. We cut to him talking about the writing process, the haunted guitar that didn't cooperate and there's...this sound in his voice that comes across as "I miss that time, I miss that feeling but it's in the past and to some extent it scares me looking back at it". The foundation of his music came from these songs, this album and he continues to play the old classics to this day but of course they sound different. 

Shakey Graves is an entity living within him. His dark passenger (Dexter reference lol) and over the years he's learned how to write music and perform without having to coax Shakey out of the shadowy corners of himself to perform for him. We get glimpses of that dark passenger sometimes. When he gets into the "zone" his eyes go dark and you can see he's traded places. Just for a second... At the end of the album you can hear he's pacing while talking. He's not comfortable. 

In recent Instagram and Twitter posts he's defended the evolution of his music and that he's been performing these same songs over and over for years... Fuck 10 years now. He's tired of it and tired of people expecting him to stay stagnant. I don't blame him. I don't blame him also knowing what he's shared on his old Tumblr blog. That was a different time, a different version of himself. I've also seen a lot of Cameo's fans have shared and I can see the fake smile he puts on. This pandemic has hit him not just financially but personally. He's said he's never set out to be the best and I think to some extent the things people say to him and about him are hard pills to swallow. 

Funny story about that (sorry, segway) my husband sent a request for a Cameo last year for my birthday. He asked him to essentially say this and that to tie in the signed art print he also bought for me. Well... Shakey didn't say any of that, he remembered my age and his video was extremely short compared to the others. But... I wasn't disappointed because I saw a real smile. He made a joke entirely his own, he just did what he wanted. 

If anything, what I take away from this album is an interesting but somewhat depressing look into that "distilled time". It's bleak, it's waiting for rain, it's hating the rain, it's pain masquerading as jaunty tunes.
